plain: Proof that someone or something was right

webster.text: The defense of any thing, or a justification against denial or censure, or against objections or accusations; as the vindication of opinions or of a creed; the vindication of the Scriptures against the objections and cavils of infidels.

more.text: The act of supporting by proof or legal process; the proving of any thing to be just; as the vindication of a title, claim or right.

example.quote: Hitherto my observations have only aimed at a vindication of the provision in question, on the ground of theoretic propriety, on that of the danger of placing the power elsewhere, and on that of the safety of placing it in the manner proposed.
